findings.summary: Role questions (hasRole family, the role and role_or_permission middleware, the @role directives, getAllPermissions) ignore throughs, ceilings and the inactive state, so a revoked or capped holder is admitted

A scope passed to can() is dropped when the check falls through to the gate hook, which answers in the ambient scope: a contract-declaring user capped to viewer in one team passes can('x', $thatTeam) on rights held in the current team
syncRoles() that changes a capped holder's role replaces the capped assignment with an uncapped one, and has no way to carry throughs: the holder ends up with more than what it acts through allows
Two routes to one role share one assignment: a capped route silently caps an existing uncapped membership, removing one route removes both, and two capped routes are AND-ed; no error tells the caller
The assignment row and its throughs are written without a transaction: a failure between the two leaves the role stored with no cap

The effective-permissions memo is reset only per HTTP request and per queue job; in any other long-lived process a role removed or a through revoked by another process keeps granting until the process exits

No test tells 'throughs are added' from 'throughs are replaced' on a re-assign (a widening mutant passes the whole suite); the memo flush after givePermissionTo and the config part of the memo key are also unpinned
harness db-check fails on the new migration: its incrementing branch gives the table a bigint primary key instead of a database-generated UUID v7
detachAllUserRoles() and userHasDirectPermission() lost their only callers in this diff and are now dead public engine methods
